draft.title: Sound and editing in film
card: comes from the world of the film, so the characters could hear it. Examples are footsteps, dialogue and a car horn.
is added over the film for the audience only, such as a music score or a narrator's voice. The characters cannot hear it.
Editing is the joining of shots with cuts. The pace is how long each shot lasts before the next cut.
Slow cuts, with long shots held on screen, can build calm or a slow dread. Quick cuts can build tension and urgency, as in a chase.
draft.remember: Diegetic sound is in the film's world, non-diegetic is added over it, and cut pace shapes tension.

a.q: In a film, a boy walks down a street. The viewer hears his footsteps and a car passing, plus a low, eerie score that he cannot hear. Which sound is non-diegetic?
opts: The eerie score
The footsteps
The passing car
The footsteps and the passing car
a.why: The score is added over the film for the audience, and the boy cannot hear it, so it is non-diegetic. The footsteps and the car are part of the street, so they are diegetic.
a.clue: Which sound could the boy not hear?

b.q: A film shows a runner chased through a market. The editor cuts between shots every half second. What is the most likely effect of this editing?
opts: It builds tension and a sense of urgency
It creates a calm, slow mood
It makes the sound non-diegetic
It lets the viewer study each detail closely
b.why: Quick cuts give the viewer little time to settle, which builds tension and urgency, as in a chase. Slow cuts would give a calmer mood and more time to study each shot. Cut pace has no effect on whether sound is diegetic.
b.clue: Think about how long the viewer has to look at each shot.

b.best: It builds tension and a sense of urgency

problems.detail: "Slow cuts, with long shots held on screen" uses "long shots" to mean shots held for a long time. In point 1 a long shot is a framing that shows setting, so students may confuse the two. Say "with each shot held on screen for longer" instead.

The stem says the score is one "he cannot hear". That repeats the card's definition of non-diegetic sound, so a student can match the words without understanding the idea. The clue repeats the giveaway.
